about: Where Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used in TERRA, for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. SI-generated images and videos carry a visible "SI-generated" watermark and a metadata note; the 3D field environment and 3D station views in the app show an on-screen "SI-generated" label.

uses.what: Large parts of the web app were written with Claude Code under the developer's direction and review: page layouts and redesigns, the 3D maps and moisture beacons, the NASA GIBS soil-moisture map, the 3D field environment, the station viewer and its exploded view (procedural parts and textures), the website with its animated logo loader, and the guided tour.
Hardware design, firmware and telemetry code, the 3D model, renders and the reveal video.
The crop renders shown throughout the app.

uses.area: Mockups, renders and videos of the app
uses.what: Device mockups, website screenshots and videos, and README images, produced by scripts written with Claude Code from the running app.
The Discovery Engine, synthetic experiments and their notes were developed with a Claude Code project setup.
README, website and in-app text, guided-tour text and the progress report were drafted with Claude Code and reviewed by the team.

30-second film: narration and sound effects generated with ElevenLabs; procedural Blender scenes and the assembly written with Claude Code; music synthesised in code. The 3D scenes are conceptual; the Rotation Lab clip is a real screen recording. Carries a visible SI-generated mark and a metadata note.

not_si.what: NASA data values themselves: retrieved from NASA services, never generated (the code that retrieves and processes them is listed above)

nasa_branding: No NASA logos, flags, insignia or mission identifiers are used or modified. "NASA" appears only as text naming the datasets used.
